To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV/HCV-coinfection is a severe form of hepatitis C with a more progredient course of the disease.
pegylated interferons are more effective than standard interferons for the treatment of hepatitis C, especially in HIV-coinfection.
The response rates of pegylated IFN and ribavirin therapy for hepatitis C in coinfected HIV/HCV patients are clearly better than under non-modified IFN/ribavirin treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new treatment strategies for the therapy of hepatitis C in patients with HIV-coinfection.
the development of treatment options which are able to achieve higher response rates than non-modified interferons in HIV/HCV co-infected patients.
the development of new treatment concepts for hepatitis C and HIV-coinfeced patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of pegylated IFN and ribavirin in HIV/HCV coinfected patients is superior to standard interferon and ribavarin in HIV/HVC-coinfected individuals.
pegylated interferons and ribavirin are the treatment of choice in HIV/HCV coinfected patients, however, further data are needed to confirm these results and to define the best treatment strategy.
the therapy of hepatitis C in coinfected HIV/HCV patients is more effective than before.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pegylated interferons and ribavirin can be used as first line therapy in HCV-coinfeted patients.
pegylated interferons are superior to standard interferons for treatment of hepatitis in HIV-coinfection.

we have to wait for results of larger studies to see if pegylated interferons and ribavirin are able to achieve sustained response rates of around or above 50% and if they are able to prevent the development of cirrhosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV/HCV- coinfection should be treated as early as possible with the new treatment regimens.
HIV infection is associated with increased risk of HCC and that the risk increases with duration of infection and with increasing age.
